headwords.definition: to exchange information, ideas, or feelings
examples: I communicate more clearly when I prepare the main point first.
The team communicates through short meetings and written updates.

headwords.definition: the process of exchanging information, meaning, or feelings
examples: Regular communication prevented the distant friends from losing touch.
Poor communication caused two departments to repeat the same work.

headwords.definition: a method or route used to communicate
examples: Email is the best channel for details that people may need later.
The emergency message was sent through several channels.

headwords.definition: involving people physically present with one another
examples: A face-to-face conversation helped us resolve the sensitive issue.
The course combines online tasks with face-to-face discussion.

headwords.definition: to send a short written message by phone
examples: I text my roommate if I will arrive late.
She texted the address so nobody had to remember it.

headwords.definition: a short written message sent electronically
examples: The text message sounded impatient because it lacked context.
I use a text message for quick changes, not serious criticism.

headwords.definition: a spoken conversation using a telephone
examples: A phone call was faster than exchanging ten confusing messages.
I schedule international phone calls because of the time difference.

headwords.definition: a recorded spoken message sent for later listening
examples: Her voice message explained the complicated directions more naturally than text.
I replayed the voice message to check the appointment time.

headwords.definition: a digital written message, especially for formal or detailed communication
examples: The email listed the deadline, attachments, and person responsible.
I reread a formal email before sending it to the professor.

headwords.definition: to answer a message, question, or request
examples: He replied to the invitation after checking his schedule.
You do not need to reply immediately to a nonurgent message.

headwords.definition: to communicate with someone, especially for a practical purpose
examples: Please contact the office if your address changes.
I contacted an old classmate through a professional network.

headwords.definition: to continue communicating with someone over time
examples: We keep in touch through monthly video calls.
Sending photographs helps the relatives keep in touch between visits.

phrases.text: The best channel depends on the purpose of the message.
I would use writing when the details need to be saved.
A quick call can prevent a long exchange of confusing texts.
Not every message requires an immediate reply.
Face-to-face contact is useful for sensitive topics.
We keep in touch through small regular updates.
The tone is harder to judge in a short message.
I choose a more formal channel for official requests.

headwords.definition: an exchange of thoughts or information between people
examples: The conversation became easier after we found a shared interest.
A private conversation was more suitable than correcting him in public.

headwords.definition: listening with full attention and showing that you are trying to understand
examples: Active listening helped the customer feel taken seriously.
The students practised active listening by summarizing a partner's point.

headwords.definition: to speak or act before someone has finished
examples: I interrupted because I misunderstood a pause as the end.
The chair politely interrupted the speaker when time expired.

headwords.definition: to do or speak one after another in an orderly way
examples: The children take turns describing their weekend.
Good video meetings require people to take turns more deliberately.

headwords.definition: a short period of silence or stopping
examples: A brief pause gave me time to organize the next sentence.
The caller interpreted the long pause as uncertainty.

headwords.definition: to answer or react to what someone says or does
examples: She responded to the concern instead of defending herself immediately.
I needed a moment before responding to the unexpected question.

headwords.definition: a question asked to obtain more detail from an earlier answer
examples: The interviewer asked a follow-up question about the example.
A thoughtful follow-up question shows genuine interest.

headwords.definition: to express the same meaning in different words
examples: I paraphrased the instructions to check that I understood them.
The teacher asked students to paraphrase the main argument.

headwords.definition: to state the main points briefly
examples: At the end, the manager summarized the decision and next steps.
Can you summarize what the customer needs before we offer a solution?

headwords.definition: giving careful and respectful attention
examples: The doctor remained attentive even when the explanation became long.
An attentive listener notices hesitation as well as words.

headwords.definition: a comfortable relationship that makes communication easier
examples: A little informal conversation built rapport before the interview.
The teacher developed rapport without pretending to be a student's friend.

phrases.text: I try to understand the point before planning my reply.
A follow-up question shows that I was listening.
I would summarize the decision before ending the conversation.
Silence can give someone time to think.
Interruptions make it difficult to develop a complete idea.
The listener should respond to what was actually said.
I might paraphrase the point to check my understanding.
Turn-taking becomes more deliberate in an online meeting.
Small signs of attention make the conversation feel less one-sided.

headwords.definition: to make a meaning, statement, or situation clearer
examples: I asked the supervisor to clarify which deadline had priority.
The speaker clarified that the figures were estimates, not final results.

headwords.definition: to make something understandable through reasons, details, or examples
examples: She explained the process with a simple diagram.
I can explain the result more easily than the technical method.

headwords.definition: brief while still including necessary information
examples: The update was concise but included every action and deadline.
A concise answer is useful when the listener already knows the background.

headwords.definition: clear and exact rather than general
examples: Specific feedback told me which sentence was confusing.
The request became easier to answer after she gave a specific date.

headwords.definition: not clear or detailed enough
examples: The vague instruction to finish soon created different expectations.
His answer remained vague because he did not want to promise a date.

headwords.definition: a particular case used to explain a general idea
examples: A familiar example made the economic concept easier to understand.
The candidate gave an example from volunteer work.

headwords.definition: a comparison used to explain how something works
examples: The teacher used a traffic analogy to explain data flow.
An analogy can simplify an idea but may hide an important difference.

headwords.definition: background information needed to understand meaning
examples: The quotation sounded rude without the context of the earlier joke.
New staff need context before they can judge why the procedure exists.

headwords.definition: the most important idea someone wants to communicate
examples: I state the main point before adding supporting detail.
The presentation's main point disappeared under too many statistics.

headwords.definition: the organized way ideas are arranged
examples: A clear structure helped the audience follow the long explanation.
The email's structure separated the problem from the requested action.

phrases.text: Let me explain that in a different way.
The main point is that the schedule has changed.
A concrete example may make the idea clearer.
I would give the necessary context before the details.
The explanation is accurate but too technical for this audience.
Could you clarify what you mean by that term?
I will separate the problem from the proposed solution.
The amount of detail depends on what the listener already knows.
A short summary can confirm that everyone understood the same decision.
The analogy is helpful up to a point.

sections.title: Tone of Voice and Body Language

headwords.definition: the quality of a voice or wording that expresses attitude or emotion
examples: Her calm tone prevented the correction from sounding hostile.
The same sentence can have a joking or serious tone.

headwords.definition: the rise and fall of the voice while speaking
examples: Rising intonation made the statement sound like a question.
Language learners practised intonation so polite requests sounded natural.

headwords.definition: how loud or quiet a voice or sound is
examples: He lowered his volume when the conversation became private.
Speaking at a steady volume helped the whole room hear.

headwords.definition: the speed at which someone speaks or an interaction develops
examples: My speaking pace becomes too fast when I am nervous.
A slower pace gave listeners time to process the instructions.

headwords.definition: meaning communicated through posture, movement, and expression
examples: Her open body language made students more willing to ask questions.
Body language varies across people and cultures, so one gesture is not proof.

headwords.definition: looking at another person's eyes or face during communication
examples: Brief eye contact showed attention without becoming uncomfortable.
Expectations about eye contact differ across cultures.

headwords.definition: a movement of the hands, head, or body that communicates meaning
examples: The guide used a hand gesture to show where visitors should wait.
A familiar gesture in one country may be rude in another.

headwords.definition: a look on the face that communicates feeling or reaction
examples: His facial expression showed confusion before he asked a question.
Video delay can make facial expressions appear unrelated to the words.

headwords.definition: the way someone holds their body
examples: Relaxed upright posture helped her breathe during the speech.
His closed posture may have reflected cold weather rather than dislike.

phrases.text: The words were polite, but the tone sounded impatient.
I slow down when I notice confused expressions.
Nonverbal cues support meaning but should not be overinterpreted.
A steady pace makes the explanation easier to follow.
Eye-contact expectations vary across cultures and individuals.
The speaker's posture became more relaxed after the opening minute.
Volume should suit the room rather than express authority.
The gesture helped direct attention to the diagram.
A delayed video image can create misleading reactions.
Tone can change how a neutral sentence is understood.
phrases.reusable_core: how a neutral sentence is understood

phrases.text: I would not judge honesty from one piece of body language.

headwords.definition: to hold a different opinion
examples: I disagree with the conclusion, but I understand the concern behind it.
The colleagues disagreed about timing rather than the goal.

headwords.definition: a situation in which people have different opinions
examples: A small disagreement became personal after an insulting comment.
The chair summarized the points of agreement before returning to the disagreement.

headwords.definition: a failure to understand meaning or intention correctly
examples: The misunderstanding came from two different uses of the word soon.
A quick call cleared up the misunderstanding.

headwords.definition: something accepted as true without checking
examples: My assumption about the deadline was wrong.
Different cultural assumptions affected how the silence was interpreted.

headwords.definition: to make someone feel hurt or insulted
examples: The joke offended him because it repeated a stereotype.
She had not intended to offend anyone and apologized directly.

headwords.definition: careful not to embarrass or upset someone unnecessarily
examples: The supervisor gave a tactful correction in private.
A tactful answer can still be honest and specific.

headwords.definition: an agreement in which different sides each accept some change
examples: The compromise kept the morning deadline but reduced the task.
Not every safety issue can be solved through compromise.

headwords.definition: to solve a disagreement, problem, or uncertainty
examples: They resolved the conflict by defining who would make the final decision.
One conversation did not resolve years of mistrust.

phrases.text: I see the issue differently for two reasons.
We agree on the goal but not the method.
Could we check what each of us understood?
I did not intend the comment in that way.
The criticism should focus on the idea rather than the person.
phrases.reusable_core: the idea rather than the person

phrases.text: A tactful response can still be direct.
I would acknowledge the valid part before explaining my concern.
The disagreement came from an unstated assumption.
Compromise is possible when both sides have flexibility.
A sincere apology can repair the immediate harm.
We may need a neutral person to guide the discussion.
Agreeing to disagree is better than repeating the same argument.

headwords.definition: the activity of exchanging short written messages by phone
examples: Texting works well for quick updates that do not need an immediate discussion.
She avoids texting while walking through crowded streets.

headwords.definition: a short written message sent by phone
examples: His text included the gate number and arrival time.
A brief text was enough to confirm the appointment.

headwords.definition: to contact someone through a digital messaging service
examples: Please message me when the meeting ends.
She messaged the class group instead of emailing each student.

headwords.definition: the amount of time someone takes to answer a message
examples: Our team agrees on a short response time for urgent safety reports.
A slow response time is normal when friends live in different time zones.

headwords.definition: to send a received digital message to another person
examples: I forwarded the confirmation email to everyone travelling with us.
She asked permission before forwarding a private message.

headwords.definition: a connected series of messages or online comments
examples: The answer was buried in a long email thread.
A separate thread kept the new issue from confusing the original discussion.

headwords.definition: an alert from a device or application
examples: I turned off notifications while preparing my presentation.
The emergency notification appeared even though the phone was silent.

headwords.definition: to stop notifications or sound temporarily
examples: She muted the group chat during her exam.
I forgot to mute my microphone before answering the door.

headwords.definition: a live conversation in which participants can see and hear one another online
examples: Our video call froze whenever someone shared a large file.
A weekly video call helps my grandparents feel connected.

headwords.definition: to understand written language or a situation incorrectly
examples: I misread his short reply as anger, although he was simply busy.
Without facial cues, jokes are easier to misread online.

headwords.definition: a small digital symbol used to express an idea or emotion
examples: She added a smiling emoji so the reminder would not sound cold.
An emoji cannot always repair an unclear or offensive message.

headwords.definition: the lasting record created by a person's online activity
examples: Teenagers should understand that an old public comment may remain in their digital footprint.
He reviewed his digital footprint before applying for internships.

phrases.text: I would send a quick message before making an unexpected call.
Short replies can sound colder than the writer intends.
The group chat is useful for updates, not private criticism.
I turn off notifications when I need sustained attention.
A video call gives us more nonverbal information.
Before forwarding a message, I check whether it is private.
Important decisions should not disappear in a long thread.
Online comments can remain visible long after the argument ends.

headwords.definition: information about what was effective and what could improve
examples: The tutor's feedback identified one strong point and one unclear paragraph.
Regular feedback helped the new employee correct mistakes early.

headwords.definition: to give someone essential information before a task
examples: The coordinator briefed volunteers on safety procedures before the event.
Please brief the afternoon team about the delayed delivery.

headwords.definition: new information about a developing situation
examples: Her morning update explained why the launch would be delayed.
We need a short update, not another full presentation.

headwords.definition: to give someone the latest information
examples: I updated my professor after the interview date changed.
The nurse updated the family when the patient left surgery.

headwords.definition: to discuss competing needs in order to reach an agreement
examples: The students negotiated a fair division of the research tasks.
She negotiated a later start date with her new employer.

headwords.definition: to give responsibility for a task to another person
examples: The team leader delegated the survey analysis to someone with statistical experience.
Good managers delegate work without disappearing from the project.

headwords.definition: to organize people or activities so they work together
examples: Two students coordinated the slides while another rehearsed the introduction.
The offices coordinate through a shared calendar and weekly call.

headwords.definition: a list of matters to discuss at a meeting
examples: The chair sent an agenda so everyone could prepare.
An urgent budget issue was added to the agenda.

headwords.definition: the written record of decisions and actions from a meeting
examples: The minutes showed that Lara had agreed to contact the supplier.
We approved last week's minutes after correcting a date.

headwords.definition: appropriate, responsible, and respectful in a work setting
examples: Her complaint remained professional even though she was frustrated.
A professional email needs a clear subject line and a specific request.

headwords.definition: scheduled times when a teacher is available to help students
examples: I used office hours to ask about feedback on my research question.
Students often avoid office hours because they think their question is too simple.

phrases.text: Could you confirm who is responsible for the next step?
I would raise the concern privately before the meeting.
The feedback is easier to use when it includes a specific example.
A written summary prevents different memories of the decision.
I need a little more context before I can answer.
We should agree on a channel for urgent messages.
The agenda keeps routine discussion from using the entire meeting.
Delegating a task does not remove responsibility for the result.
I would ask for feedback while there is still time to revise.

headwords.definition: the people watching or listening to a talk or performance
examples: The audience included new students who did not know the technical terms.
She adjusted her examples after noticing the audience's puzzled reaction.

headwords.definition: a planned talk that explains or reports something to a group
examples: Our presentation used one graph to support the main claim.
He rehearsed the presentation aloud rather than silently reading the slides.

headwords.definition: to explain information or ideas formally to an audience
examples: I will present our findings at Friday's seminar.
She presented the proposal without reading every sentence from the screen.

headwords.definition: to practise something before performing it publicly
examples: We rehearsed with a timer and shortened the final section.
He rehearsed the opening until he could make eye contact naturally.

headwords.definition: a short organized plan showing the main parts of a talk or text
examples: A one-page outline kept me from losing my place.
The outline put the recommendation before the supporting evidence.

headwords.definition: one screen in a digital presentation
examples: The slide showed the trend with a labelled line graph.
Too much text on each slide made the audience read instead of listen.

headwords.definition: an image, object, chart, or other visual support for a talk
examples: A map was the most useful visual aid for explaining the route.
The speaker removed a decorative visual aid that distracted from the data.

headwords.definition: nervousness about speaking or performing before an audience
examples: My stage fright is strongest during the minute before I begin.
Repeated classroom talks gradually reduced her stage fright.

headwords.definition: to stop speaking briefly and intentionally
examples: I paused after the main result so listeners could absorb it.
She paused to find the right word instead of filling the silence with um.

headwords.definition: to use the voice strongly enough to be heard clearly
examples: The coach taught us to project without shouting.
He projected his voice toward the back of the hall.

phrases.text: I would open with a question that the talk will answer.
phrases.reusable_core: a question that the talk will answer

phrases.text: The slides should support the speaker rather than replace the speaker.
A short pause can emphasize an important result.
I practise aloud because silent rehearsal hides timing problems.
The audience needs a clear sign when the topic changes.
One concrete example is more memorable than five abstract claims.
If I lose my place, I return to the outline.
Nervousness usually decreases after I finish the opening.
Questions reveal which parts of the explanation were unclear.
phrases.reusable_core: which parts of the explanation were unclear

phrases.text: I would end by restating the action I want listeners to take.
phrases.reusable_core: the action I want listeners to take

headwords.definition: able to communicate smoothly and effectively in a language
examples: She is fluent enough to lead meetings, although she still checks legal terms.
Regular conversation made him more fluent than grammar exercises alone.

headwords.definition: the ability to communicate smoothly without excessive hesitation
examples: Recording short answers helped me notice improvements in fluency.
Fluency does not require a perfect accent or error-free grammar.

headwords.definition: the way words and sounds are spoken
examples: Clear pronunciation matters more than copying one particular accent.
I checked the pronunciation after listeners confused ship with sheep.

headwords.definition: a recognizable way of pronouncing a language associated with a place or group
examples: Her accent shows where she grew up but does not prevent understanding.
People sometimes unfairly judge intelligence from an unfamiliar accent.

headwords.definition: the words and phrases a person knows or uses
examples: Reading news about one topic helped me build useful vocabulary in context.
A large passive vocabulary does not automatically produce fluent speech.

headwords.definition: the strategy of describing an idea when the exact word is unavailable
examples: Circumlocution helped me describe a kettle when I forgot its English name.
Too much circumlocution can confuse listeners if a simple familiar word is available.

headwords.definition: to involve yourself deeply in a language or environment
examples: She immersed herself in Spanish through local clubs and daily radio.
You can create partial immersion even if you cannot travel abroad.

headwords.definition: to change spoken or written meaning from one language into another
examples: I translated the instructions for my grandparents at the clinic.
Word-for-word translation made the idiom sound strange.

headwords.definition: to change language or language variety according to the situation or audience
examples: My cousins code-switch between Persian and English during family dinners.
Employees may code-switch to match formal and informal settings.

phrases.text: I focus on being understood rather than hiding my accent.
If I forget a word, I explain the idea another way.
Short daily practice is easier to maintain than rare long sessions.
Mistakes show me which part of the language needs attention.
I learn phrases in situations where I might actually use them.
phrases.reusable_core: where I might actually use them

phrases.text: Listening becomes difficult when speakers reduce familiar words.
A conversation partner gives me a reason to respond in real time.
Translation is useful, but it cannot explain every cultural meaning.
Progress is easier to notice in recordings made several months apart.
I would ask the speaker to slow down without apologizing repeatedly.
Using simple language accurately is better than forcing impressive vocabulary.

headwords.definition: a behavior or expectation widely considered usual within a cultural group
examples: Removing shoes indoors is a cultural norm in many households.
A cultural norm describes a tendency, not every individual.

headwords.definition: an oversimplified belief about all members of a group
examples: The training challenged the stereotype that quiet employees lack ideas.
One friendly encounter cannot confirm a national stereotype.

headwords.definition: to understand the meaning or intention of something
examples: Visitors interpreted the long silence in different ways.
I try not to interpret indirect language as dishonesty.

headwords.definition: welcoming and allowing different people to participate
examples: An inclusive discussion gives quieter members time to enter.
The host used inclusive language that did not assume everyone had children.

headwords.definition: to change behavior or methods to suit a new situation
examples: She adapted her humor when working with an international team.
I can adapt to local customs without pretending to share every belief.

headwords.definition: belief in one's ability to act or speak effectively
examples: Preparation gave me enough confidence to ask the first question.
His confidence grew through small conversations, not motivational advice alone.

headwords.definition: uncomfortably worried about how other people see you
examples: I felt self-conscious about my pauses during the first language exchange.
A supportive partner made her less self-conscious about mistakes.

headwords.definition: friendly and easy to speak to or ask for help
examples: The professor seemed more approachable after inviting questions informally.
Open posture can make a receptionist look approachable, but clear words matter too.

phrases.text: I would observe first instead of assuming my habit is universal.
A cultural pattern should not become a judgment about an individual.
When I am unsure, a respectful question is safer than a guess.
Inclusive groups make room for people who need more time to respond.
Confidence grows through manageable interactions.
I can adapt my style without losing my personality.
Humor is difficult to transfer across languages and cultures.
An unfamiliar communication style is not automatically rude.
I would learn the person's preference rather than rely on a stereotype.
phrases.reusable_core: rather than rely on a stereotype

phrases.text: Shared tasks can make first conversations feel less forced.
It is reasonable to explain my own boundary politely.
Curiosity works best when it is paired with respect.
